description: Core AUZiX packages that should be validated before the next ISO rebuild. These are installer/runtime spine packages, not desktop demo extras.

batches.purpose: Make disk discovery, partitioning, formatting, repair, and resizing native enough that the installer does not fall back to BusyBox ext2.

packages.notes: Source recipe exists but was missing from the repo seen by vmid135. This must be present before partition/format so fresh installs use ext4.
Needed for EFI/system partitions and removable media repair.
Installer and control panel need real block-device and mount introspection, not only BusyBox fallbacks.
Prefer GPT-aware partitioning for future EFI, LVM, ZFS, and larger disk layouts.
Desktop proof tool after the storage CLI spine is real.

batches.purpose: Make the installer able to bring up wired or wifi networking, verify TLS, and fetch repo updates before or during install.

packages.notes: Required for reliable route/interface inspection and future bridge/container networking diagnostics.
BusyBox udhcpc is acceptable initially, but AUZiX should own the DHCP service contract and receipts.
If the install target is wifi-only, the live installer needs scan/connect flows before package refresh or updates can work.
Pick one higher-level network manager later. For now, define the low-level wifi/runtime packages first.
Required before HTTPS repo refresh, Git, Flatpak, curl, browser, and package validation.
Installer update probes should prefer AUZiX curl and fall back to BusyBox wget only for recovery.

batches.purpose: Prepare network-backed install/update paths and future advanced disk layouts without forcing all of it into the first minimal ISO.

packages.notes: Needed for lab-build/ns1 package mirrors, rescue installs, and mounted build assets.
SMB client mount support for office/lab shares.
Optional first, but common enough that installer partition logic should account for it.
Potentially useful but license/kernel-module implications make this an explicit evaluation lane, not a hidden dependency.

batches.purpose: Stop smoke tests from lying by ensuring clean installs have enough native diagnostics to explain failures.

packages.notes: Clean vmid135 lacked enough standalone utilities; package scripts should not assume host-like /usr tools.
Needed for memory/swap/process diagnostics and control panel health reports.
Used by package validation to classify ELF/script/text payloads.
Already visible on vmid135; keep it in the clean-install proof set.

batches.purpose: Make AUZiX installer/live media generation a package-built lane instead of a one-off shell artifact.

packages.notes: Debian/Trixie package that creates live system images. Use as the first reference for AUZiX package-group-driven ISO assembly.
Already used by current ISO patch scripts; promote to an explicit AUZiX package/receipt before the next media-builder pipeline.
Required for live root creation and validation.
BIOS boot asset package used by live media builders.
ISOLINUX boot files for legacy BIOS ISO paths.
BIOS GRUB image tooling for installer/live media.
EFI boot image tooling for amd64 installer/live media.
Needed for FAT/EFI image assembly without loop-mount side effects.
Reference package for Debian installer media construction; evaluate patterns but do not let it own AUZiX layout.
Reference package for custom Debian installer media/profile ideas.

before_next_iso: Published repo contains all installer-core packages marked must-publish.
A clean vmid135 install can refresh packages, install E2fsprogs, and create an ext4 test image.
auzix-install-disk either finds mkfs.ext4 in the live root or has a documented bootstrap path before formatting.
Pipeline rejects packages listed as installable when their dependency closure is absent from the repo index.
WifiRuntime has at least a package-level plan and command presence test, even if GUI connection management waits.
Installer media generation has a package group and can identify live-build/xorriso/squashfs/bootloader tooling as AUZiX package targets.
